headline: Huang quits Nvidia and oil jumps on Iran; S&P 500 −0.35% as the 10-year hits 5.10%
summary: Stocks opened sharply lower after Nvidia announced Jensen Huang's resignation (S&P 500 −0.9%, Nasdaq −1.6% early), clawed back to small gains by late morning (S&P high 7,649.21) as Nvidia halved its loss, then faded through the afternoon as Treasury yields climbed. Breadth was weak: the equal-weight S&P fell about 0.9%, decliners outnumbered advancers roughly 2.6 to 1 in the index, and energy was the only sector to gain while small caps lost 1.7%.
drivers: Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Huang stepped down amid the board probe; the stock fell as much as 14% to $148.80 at the open before closing −4.3% at $166.19, about 31% below its October record, the biggest single drag on the S&P 500 (roughly −0.2 point). Nvidia-linked AI clouds slid: Nebius −16.8% after pushing some 2026 revenue into next year and raising spending plans, CoreWeave −6.9%, Super Micro −11.3%.
Money rotates to Nvidia's rivals, chips split

AMD rose 5.9%, Broadcom 5.5%, Arista 5.1% and Alphabet 1.8% on hopes they gain share, nearly offsetting Nvidia's drag. The SOX still slipped 0.54% after a 17% four-day surge, with 24 of 30 members down: Applied Materials −3.6% before its results, Sandisk −4.1%, Intel −2.0%, Micron −1.6%.
Trump's Iran post lifts oil and yields

Trump said the US no longer needs a deal with Iran, and attacks on Saudi energy sites added to supply worries: WTI settled +2.6% at $88.74 and Brent +3.3% at $95.82. With bonds reopening after Veterans Day, the 10-year yield rose about 11bp to 5.10%, its highest since Oct 21, and the dollar hit a 19-month high; energy (XLE +1.5%) was the only gaining sector while airlines fell (United −6.0%, Delta −5.2%).
Hike bets weigh on small caps and rate-sensitives

Futures fully price a December Fed hike with about 15% odds of a half point after this week's hot CPI; the Fed's Daly said more hikes are likely, while Hammack saw no need to move faster. Jobless claims rose to 200,000 and October existing-home sales hit their slowest pace since 2010; the Russell 2000 fell 1.7%, and Global Payments sank 12% after buyout talks ended.
week: Week to date the S&P 500 is up 2.9%, the Nasdaq 3.2%, the Dow 2.0% and the Russell 2000 1.6%, leaving the S&P 500 about 3% below its October record, with a December Fed hike fully priced and the 10-year yield back above 5%.
watch: Next: October PPI on Friday; after Thursday's close Cisco rose about 5% after hours on a beat and raised outlook while Applied Materials swung after a beat-and-raise; Nvidia reports Tue Nov 17, Anthropic's IPO prices Nov 18, and the Fed meets Dec 8–9.
